transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

I’m here because everybody keeps acting like I’m making this up, but I’m not. My wife’s relative has been coming into the house to get at me. My tools don’t just move on their own, and my fishing plans don’t get ruined every weekend by accident. This has been going on for months, and it’s clear to me he’s trying to take over my place and push me out.
Over these past few months, have you also noticed changes in your mood—like feeling unusually sad, hopeless, or on the other hand, unusually energetic, elated, or needing much less sleep than normal?

I don’t know… I wouldn’t say I’ve been unusually sad or anything like that. And I’m not walking around feeling great or full of energy either. I sleep about how I usually do, I guess. I’m mostly just dealing with what’s been happening.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that others couldn't hear, or seen things that weren't really there?
No, I don’t think so. I mean, I hear normal sounds, like around the house or outside, but not voices or seeing things that aren’t there. That’s not what this is.
Do you have any medical conditions—like a head injury, seizures, thyroid problems, or other neurological issues—or do you use alcohol or any recreational drugs?
Not that I know of. I mean, I haven’t had anything like that diagnosed. I don’t use drugs. I might have a drink now and then, but nothing that would explain what’s been going on.
How long exactly have you been noticing these things—your tools moving, your fishing plans being ruined, and your belief that your wife's relative is trying to push you out?
It’s been about nine months now. It started around when my wife’s relative moved into our home, and since then I’ve been noticing these things happening.
Over these past nine months, has this situation affected your ability to work, manage your usual responsibilities, or keep up with your daily routine?

No, not really. I still get up and go to the plant, do my assembler work, pay the bills, keep myself together like I always have. It’s more that the trouble is at home, with him and my things. That’s where it all centers.
